newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Kenyan elephants ignore frontier to raid farms.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan elephants ignore frontier to raid farms.

text.p: A border-hopping group of Kenyan elephants has caused a swathe of damage in a Tanzanian village, squashing food crops and laying waste to acres of land, the semi-official Sunday News reported.

About 15 elephants left the game reserve in nearby Kenya and romped through Rombo district in Tanzania's northern Kilimanjaro region, flattening plots of maize, millet, sunflower, cassava and pigeon peas, the newspaper said.
Rombo district commissioner Peniel Saitabau said the animals were causing widespread grief for hundreds of local villagers, already battling the effects of a widespread drought.
He said four government game scouts had been deployed to try to chase the elephants back into Kenya. In 1994 after a similar rampage in Rombo, game wardens were forced to shoot and kill 17 elephants.
